required_gaps: Observe recovery with B substituted during retirement, B's interrupted publication failing, and C queued. Also verify B's owner-facing result on successful recovery.
Verify one interrupted archive across repeated polls of a locked claim recovered by a fresh session.
Exercise a change to the completed pending archive before its rename and an actual private-payload write or flush failure before retry.
source_inspection_only: The loss on a failed late-replacement commit, repeated interrupted archives, missing result for B and mutable pending-file interval follow from the production control flow. The recorded cases do not exercise those outcomes.
Commit writes and flushes the private payload before moving it. The recorded R4-F1 obstruction occurs after both operations succeed.

findings.actual: Opening B with FileOptions.DeleteOnClose commits to deleting it before ReadAll, Digest or Commit succeeds. If the interrupted archive cannot be published, disposing the handle still deletes B. The next poll can take C with only A's archive present.
findings.blocking_rationale: Cleanup for A can permanently consume B's repair request without a durable disposition.
findings.expected: A failure while identifying or preserving B leaves its exact bytes discoverable for recovery before C is admitted.
findings.requested_correction: Make deletion conditional on verifying the contents of the held file. Leave a replacement recoverable through its own result and archive publication.
findings.requested_evidence: Replace A with B at BeforeRetire, queue C and obstruct B's interrupted archive. Verify B survives the failure. Exercise same-session and fresh-session recovery, then show B settled before C runs and A removed exactly once.
findings.title: A failed interruption archive still deletes the replacement claim
findings.trigger: B replaces A between the first exclusive read and the deleting open, then reading B or committing its interrupted archive fails.

findings.actual: The unowned-claim branch clears the session and calls Close without passing an archive record. Each poll writes the interrupted result and commits another archive before the exclusive open fails again.
findings.blocking_rationale: A single stranded request can create a new terminal file every two seconds for the duration of the lock.
findings.expected: After the first interrupted archive commits, subsequent polls retry only retirement.
findings.requested_correction: Retain the interrupted decision and committed archive identity across polls, including when the current session first discovers an unowned claim.
findings.requested_evidence: Start a fresh session with a stranded .claimed file held with FileShare.Read and a newer request waiting. Poll repeatedly, release the handle and verify one interrupted archive, zero removals for the stranded claim and normal processing of the waiting request.
findings.title: A locked claim recovered after restart republishes its interrupted archive
findings.trigger: A fresh session finds a readable .claimed file whose existing reader prevents exclusive retirement.

findings.actual: Commit closes the exclusive stream after Flush(true), then File.Move resolves the pending filename again. A change to that file in the interval publishes the changed contents under A's terminal suffix. The existing replacement tests edit .claimed and leave this new source untouched.
findings.blocking_rationale: An applied archive can identify a different request from the one whose horse was changed.
findings.expected: The terminal rename publishes the exact payload bound to A's decision, or fails with A's claim available for retry.
findings.requested_correction: Keep the completed staging file's identity and contents protected through terminal publication.
findings.requested_evidence: At BeforeCommit, attempt to edit or replace the actual .pending file. Verify the change is excluded or publication stops safely, then check the final archive byte-for-byte against A and confirm one removal.
findings.title: The pending archive can change between flush and publication
findings.trigger: A writer changes the completed .pending file after its stream closes and before the terminal move.

findings.actual: The late-mismatch branch commits B's bytes directly with InterruptedSuffix and returns to A's publication. The result file still says Applied for A. Once B is deleted, no later poll can report its interruption.
findings.blocking_rationale: The owner loses the result explaining that B was untouched and requires a new request, even when all file operations succeed.
findings.expected: B receives an interrupted result naming B and explaining how to retry, consistent with the other replacement-claim path.
findings.requested_correction: Route B through the policy's interrupted reporting path so its result and archive are both completed.
findings.requested_evidence: Extend the successful BeforeRetire replacement case to inspect the result before a queued C runs. Verify it names B as interrupted, A's applied archive still holds A, and B's fact remains present.
findings.title: A replacement archived during retirement receives no owner-facing result
findings.trigger: The final deleting open finds B and the inline interrupted archive succeeds.

findings.actual: FailedCommitLeavesNoPartialArchive creates a directory at the terminal name after the private write and flush have succeeded. It exercises a failed move and a successful retry. It never faults the write or flush requested in R4-F1.
findings.blocking_rationale: The source addresses partial publication on this path, but the requested failure observation is absent.
findings.expected: A failure during private-payload write or flush leaves no partial terminal archive, and retry produces exactly one complete archive.
findings.requested_correction: Exercise a failure after private file creation during the payload write or flush. Retain the existing final-move obstruction case.
findings.requested_evidence: Record the failed poll with the claim present and no terminal archive. After retry, assert one terminal archive with the original raw bytes and one removal in total.
findings.title: The archive test faults the rename after a successful flush
findings.trigger: Assessing the requested R4-F1 evidence for a partial write or failed flush.

prior_finding_assessments.rationale: MessageOf contains the throwing Message getter on the native and feature-read failure paths. The recorded case applied once, archived A's request and preserved the reloaded fact across subsequent same-session and fresh-session polls.

The settlement rename that stranded a claim under an undiscoverable name is gone. The recorded same-session and fresh-session cases found B at .claimed and settled it before C. R4-F3 covers the separate loss during the later deleting open.
The private-file implementation puts the terminal move after a successful write, flush and close. The remaining gap is evidence. The recorded test obstructed the move after a complete flush.
The applied-claim sharing test passed with one archive. Interrupted recovery bypasses the new session record, so the same denied retirement still republishes that claim on every poll.
The late-replacement test preserved B when its interrupted commit succeeded. DeleteOnClose still disposes of B if that commit throws, before B has a recoverable disposition.
